directAnswer: Pope John XIX (reigned 1024–1032), born Romanus of Tusculum, succeeded his brother Benedict VIII while still a layman. He crowned Conrad II emperor in 1027 before King Cnut of England and invited the music teacher Guido of Arezzo to Rome to present his new system of notation.

sections.h2: From Consul and Senator to Pope
paras: Romanus, a son of Count Gregory of Tusculum, held the civil leadership of Rome during his brother's pontificate, with titles such as consul and senator. When Benedict VIII died in April 1024, Romanus was elected to succeed him. Because he was a layman, he received all the clerical orders in rapid succession. Contemporary writers criticized the election as a family arrangement secured through influence and money.

The succession kept the papacy firmly in Tusculan hands. Another brother, Alberic III, held the leading position among the family's lay members, and it was his son who would follow John on the papal throne. For eight years the city's civil and spiritual leadership were again concentrated in a single household.

The Burgundian chronicler Rodulfus Glaber reports that in 1024 envoys of the Byzantine emperor and Patriarch Eustathius asked John to recognize the patriarch of Constantinople as universal within his own sphere, offering generous gifts. According to Glaber, protests from Western churchmen and monks led John to drop the proposal. The episode is known only from Glaber and some related sources, so details remain uncertain.

On Easter Day, 26 March 1027, John crowned Conrad II emperor and his wife Gisela empress in St. Peter's. The ceremony was attended by King Cnut of England and Denmark and King Rudolph III of Burgundy. Cnut later wrote that he used the visit to obtain reduced fees for English archbishops receiving the pallium and protection for English pilgrims traveling to Rome.
John's cooperation with Conrad continued in other matters, including disputes between the patriarchates of Aquileia and Grado, in which papal decisions shifted with the political situation.

sections.h2: Guido of Arezzo and Musical Notation
paras: Around 1028 John invited Guido of Arezzo, a Benedictine music teacher, to Rome. Guido had developed a system of lines and spaces that let singers learn chant much faster than by memory alone. According to Guido's own letter, the pope examined his antiphonary and was able to sing a melody he had never heard before. John's endorsement helped the new method gain acceptance.
John XIX died in October 1032. His nephew Theophylact succeeded him as Benedict IX.

keyFacts: Born Romanus, brother of Benedict VIII; a layman when elected
Crowned Conrad II emperor on Easter 1027, with Cnut present
Cnut secured lower pallium fees for English archbishops
Invited Guido of Arezzo to Rome and endorsed his musical notation

faqs.question: Why was John XIX's election criticized?
faqs.answer: He was a layman from the ruling Tusculan family who succeeded his own brother, and contemporaries believed influence and money secured his election.

faqs.question: How did John XIX support Guido of Arezzo?
faqs.answer: He brought Guido to Rome around 1028 and examined his new notation system. Guido reported that the pope sang an unfamiliar melody at sight using it.

faqs.question: Which kings attended Conrad II's coronation by John XIX?
faqs.answer: King Cnut of England and Denmark and King Rudolph III of Burgundy attended the Easter 1027 coronation.
